speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following treatment for sinusitis; can you describe the nature and severity of the flank pain? Have you noticed any changes in your urination, such as frequency, burning, or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms persisting after sinusitis improvement suggests a possible kidney infection or other systemic issue. Do you have any nausea, vomiting, or pain when urinating, and have you had any recent procedures or catheter use?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text:
It is concerning that you developed a rash with amoxicillin, as this could indicate an allergic reaction or drug-induced interstitial nephritis. To help distinguish between these possibilities, have you noticed any swelling in your legs, face, or around your eyes?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_and_Microscopy
REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine_and_BUN

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis_and_Microscopy: Leukocyturia present, Bacterial Culture negative, Cytospin Stained With Hansel’s Solution shows 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm (eosinophils). Serum_Creatinine_and_BUN: Creatinine Elevated, Urea (BUN) Elevated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of eosinophils in the urine, combined with elevated creatinine and a history of recent antibiotic use and rash, strongly points to acute interstitial nephritis. Do you have any joint pain or skin rash currently?

REQUEST TEST: Serum_IgE_Level
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal IgE levels and lack of current rash or joint pain make systemic allergic causes less likely, reinforcing the diagnosis of drug-induced acute interstitial nephritis. I have sufficient evidence to conclude. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
